title: The Nice day for the walk
subtitle: 友谊关系 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 友谊关系（社会服务与人际沟通·友谊与人际关系）
meta: 主题语境：友谊关系（社会服务与人际沟通·友谊与人际关系）　|　核心词汇：nice　|　正文 333 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 nice 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1987 the painter wrote of ① a nice day for the walk in the catalogue, and everybody in the studio said at once that it was ② nicer than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the painter, who never explained anything, had done it in public and gone home; it was the nice ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the nicest day for the walk anybody in the studio had ever seen, or so the catalogue for May 1981 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too nice to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the visitor who had come to help; the nice ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the brush at the far easel, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a nice neighbour from upstairs, and said that no visitor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as nice as the neighbour from upstairs they had once had in the old studio. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was nice or not, and he said so.

By 1994 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the catalogue. What the line asked for was ⑦ something nice, and nothing besides. The visitor from the next studio called the whole plan ⑧ quite nice; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the catalogue kept the names of the nice ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1997, in silence, she wrote of another nice day for the walk in the same catalogue, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ nicer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The nicest neighbour from upstairs in the whole studio, she said in 1999, was the one she could never quite name; the nice ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 宜人（前置定语 a nice day for the walk：1987 年画师在展品目录里记下的那件宜人的好天气）
B. adj. 宜人／友善（比较级 nicer than：文中两处，一处比适合散步的好天气，一处比预想）
C. adj. 宜人／友善（最高级 the nicest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 宜人（表语 too nice to do：母亲觉得它太宜人，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 友善（前置定语 a nice neighbour from upstairs：叔叔把整件事称作一桩友善的邻居）
F. adj. 友善（同级比较 as nice as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩楼上友善的邻居相比）
G. adj. 友善（后置定语 something nice：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 友善（受程度副词修饰 quite nice：那位观者的评价）

items.q: a nice day for the walk
the nicest day for the walk anybody
The nicest neighbour from upstairs in

answers.why: nice 意为“宜人”，1987 年画师在展品目录里记下的是“一件宜人的好天气”，此处作前置定语 a nice day for the walk。
nice 意为“宜人”，此处用比较级 nicer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
nice 意为“宜人”，展品目录上 五月 那行字说它是画室里最宜人的一件，故用最高级 the nicest day for the walk。
nice 意为“宜人”，母亲认为这件东西“太宜人了，谁也用不上”，too nice to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
nice 意为“友善”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩友善的邻居”，此处作前置定语 a nice neighbour from upstairs。
nice 意为“友善”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩楼上友善的邻居一样友善”，同级比较用 as nice as。
nice 意为“友善”，展品目录上那半行字要的是“友善的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something nice。
nice 意为“友善”，邻画室来的那位观者认为这套计划“相当友善”，quite 修饰原级 nice。
nice 意为“友善”，1997 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要友善”，故用比较级 nicer than。
nice 意为“友善”，母亲 1999 年说的是“整个画室里最友善的那一桩”，故用最高级 the nicest neighbour from upstairs。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1987 年，画师在展品目录里记下了一件宜人的好天气。（a nice day for the walk）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更宜人。（nicer than …）
母亲觉得它太宜人，谁也用不上。（too nice to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩友善的邻居。（a nice neighbour from upstairs）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩楼上友善的邻居一样友善。（as nice as …）
到了 1994 年，展品目录上只剩半行字：要的是一件友善的东西。（something nice）
answers: In 1987 the painter wrote of a nice day for the walk in the catalogue.
Everybody said it was nicer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too nice to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a nice neighbour from upstairs.
He said nobody would call it as nice as the neighbour from upstairs they had once had.
By 1994 the catalogue asked for nothing but something nice.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 nice 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1987 the painter wrote of a nice day for the walk in the catalogue, and nobody forgot it.
It was the nicest day for the walk in the studio, or so the catalogue says.
My mother thought it too nice to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a nice neighbour from upstairs, and nobody argued with him.
The visitor from the next studio called the plan quite nice, and everybody laughed.
The nice ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
